name: Sat Kartar Life Ltd
tagline: NSE-SME D2C Ayurveda brand (revenue ~4x in 4 years) pivoting to an asset-light 'specialised Ayurvedic hospital' model with an infertility niche — interesting optionality, but a single un-validated forum post, promoter-only projections and an unproven hospital pivot
business_overview: Direct-to-consumer Ayurvedic wellness company (flagship Sat Kartar brand, Rs 3,000-4,000 ticket; mass-market via subsidiary Ajooni Lifesciences). Some backward integration (in-house powder manufacturing; acquired Phantomed Nutraceuticals for ~50% in-house capsules). Stated strategy: reuse the D2C patient funnel, data and trained call-centre team to build a network of small (~30-bed) asset-light hospitals (~Rs 7-8 lakh/bed) focused on Ayurvedic infertility treatment (~80% of revenue at its existing 30-bed Delhi facility).
fundamentals_table: Rs 51.9 Cr FY22 -> ~Rs 194-200 Cr FY26 (~+18% YoY latest)
~Rs 1,034 Cr revenue by FY30 (base case) — unverified
fundamentals_narrative: The core D2C business has scaled ~4x in four years and turned more profitable, which is real. The re-rating case rests on the hospital pivot: asset-light bed economics, an under-served Ayurvedic-infertility niche, and operating leverage from an existing (post-conversion) call-centre. But the pivot is essentially unproven beyond one 30-bed Delhi unit; the FY30 revenue projection is internal/promoter; D2C Ayurveda is intensely competitive (Patanjali, Dabur, dozens of D2C brands); and the claim that Ayurvedic infertility treatment has better success rates than IVF is, by the forum author's own admission, unbacked by data.
sentiment_summary: Effectively no community view: the thread is a single detailed write-up (Sep 2026) by a non-trusted user plus two image-only posts. No discussion, no counter-view, no trusted call.
community_signal: None. Discovery candidate, theme-rank 1 (priority-2 theme 'single-speciality hospitals & diagnostics', keyword 'hospital').
